title: Understanding PHP Performance
learning_outcomes: Explain what understanding php performance contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: execution time.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Performance work starts with a measurable target and representative workload. Profile before changing code, compare the same conditions after a change, and consider memory, cache invalidation, and regression risk. In this lesson, focus on execution time; then compare it with memory consumption. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use understanding php performance when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Performance work starts with a measurable target and representative workload. Profile before changing code, compare the same conditions after a change, and consider memory, cache invalidation, and regression risk. For understanding php performance, begin with execution time. Also distinguish memory consumption; request throughput; startup and application overhead. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content_blocks.title: Walk through one example
content_blocks.text: Read the example for understanding php performance from top to bottom. common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
